records.Description: Icon-only buttons must expose an accessible label
records.Do: Set accessibilityLabel or label prop on icon buttons
records.Keywords: icon button accessibilityLabel

records.Description: All inputs must have a visible label and an accessibility label
records.Do: Pair Text label with input and set accessibilityLabel
records.Keywords: form input label accessibilityLabel

records.Description: Interactive elements must expose correct roles/traits
records.Don't: Rely on generic views with no roles
records.Keywords: accessibilityRole accessibilityTraits

records.Description: Async status updates should be announced to screen readers
records.Don't: Update text silently with no announcement
records.Keywords: accessibilityLiveRegion announce

records.Description: Decorative icons should be hidden from screen readers
records.Do: Mark decorative icons as not accessible
records.Don't: Have screen reader read every icon
records.Keywords: accessible={false} importantForAccessibility

records.Description: Primary touch targets must be at least 44x44pt
records.Do: Increase hitSlop or padding to meet minimum
records.Don't: Small icons with tiny touch area
records.Keywords: touch 44x44 hitSlop

records.Description: Adjacent touch targets need enough spacing
records.Do: Keep at least 8dp spacing between touchables
records.Don't: Cluster many buttons with no gap
records.Keywords: touch spacing gap 8px

records.Description: Custom gestures must not break system scroll/back
records.Don't: Full-screen custom swipe conflicting with back
records.Keywords: scroll swipe back gesture

records.Description: Back navigation should be predictable and preserve state
records.Do: Use navigation.goBack and keep screen state
records.Don't: Reset stack or exit app unexpectedly
records.Keywords: back handler navigation stack

records.Description: Bottom tab bar should have at most 5 primary items
records.Do: Use 3–5 tabs and move extras to More/Settings
records.Don't: Overloaded tab bar with many icons
records.Keywords: tab bar max items

records.Description: Modals/sheets must have clear close actions
records.Do: Provide close button and swipe-down where platform expects
records.Don't: Trapping users in modal with no obvious exit
records.Keywords: modal dismiss close affordance

records.Description: Returning to a screen should restore its scroll and form state
records.Do: Keep components mounted or persist state
records.Don't: Reset list scroll and form inputs on every visit
records.Keywords: navigation preserve state

records.Description: Show visible feedback during network operations
records.Do: Use ActivityIndicator or skeleton for >300ms operations
records.Keywords: activity indicator skeleton

records.Description: Confirm successful actions with brief feedback
records.Don't: Complete actions silently with no confirmation
records.Keywords: toast checkmark banner

records.Description: Show clear error messages near the problem
records.Don't: Only change border color with no explanation
records.Keywords: inline error banner

records.Description: Validate inputs on blur or submit with clear messaging
records.Don't: Validate on every keystroke causing jank
records.Keywords: onBlur validation

records.Description: Use appropriate keyboardType and returnKeyType
records.Don't: Use default keyboard for all inputs
records.Keywords: keyboardType returnKeyType

records.Description: Guide users through form fields with Next/Done flows
records.Do: Use onSubmitEditing to focus next input
records.Don't: Force users to tap each field manually
records.Keywords: autoFocus blurOnSubmit onSubmitEditing

records.Description: Allow toggling password visibility securely
records.Don't: Force users to type blind with no option
records.Keywords: secureTextEntry toggle

records.Description: Use FlatList/SectionList for lists over ~50 items
records.Don't: Render hundreds of items with ScrollView
records.Keywords: FlatList SectionList virtualization

records.Description: Use correctly sized and cached images
records.Do: Use Image component with proper resizeMode and caching
records.Keywords: Image resize cache

records.Description: Debounce scroll/search callbacks to avoid jank
records.Don't: Run heavy logic on every event
records.Keywords: debounce scroll search

records.Description: Micro-interactions should be 150–300ms with native-like easing
records.Do: Use ease-out for enter/ease-in for exit
records.Don't: Use long or linear animations for core UI
records.Keywords: animation duration easing

records.Description: Respect OS reduced-motion accessibility setting
records.Keywords: reduced motion accessibility

records.Description: Reserve infinite animations for loaders and live data
records.Keywords: loop animation loader

records.Description: Body text must be readable and support Dynamic Type
records.Do: Use platform fontScale and at least 14–16pt base
records.Keywords: fontScale dynamic type

records.Description: Support system text scaling without breaking layout
records.Do: Set allowFontScaling and test large text
records.Don't: Disable scaling on all text globally
records.Keywords: allowFontScaling adjustsFontSizeToFit

records.Description: Content must not overlap notches/gesture bars
records.Do: Wrap screens in SafeAreaView or apply insets
records.Don't: Place tappable content under system bars
records.Keywords: safe area insets notch gesture

records.Description: Ensure sufficient contrast in both light and dark themes
records.Do: Use semantic tokens and test both themes
records.Don't: Reuse light-theme grays directly in dark mode
records.Keywords: dark mode contrast tokens

records.Description: Don't rely solely on hidden gestures for core actions
records.Do: Provide visible buttons in addition to gestures
records.Don't: Rely on swipe/shake only with no UI affordance
records.Keywords: gesture only hidden controls

records.A11y Fallback: Dashed/dotted lines per series; togglable data table with timestamps and values
records.Accessibility Notes: Differentiate series by line style (solid/dashed/dotted) not color alone. Add pattern overlays for colorblind users.
records.Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
records.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
records.Keywords: trend, time-series, line, growth, timeline, progress
records.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
records.When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period

records.A11y Fallback: Value labels always visible; provide CSV export
records.Accessibility Notes: Value labels on each bar by default. Sort control for user reordering.
records.Color Guidance: Each bar: distinct color. Grouped: same hue family. Always sort descending by value
records.Data Volume Threshold: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20–50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
records.Keywords: compare, categories, bar, comparison, ranking
records.When NOT to Use: Categories > 15 (use table or search); data has time dimension (use line); showing proportions (use waffle/stacked)
records.When to Use: Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories ≤ 15

records.A11y Fallback: Must provide stacked bar alternative + percentage data table as mandatory fallback
records.Accessibility Notes: Pie charts fail WCAG for colorblind users. Slices rely on color alone. Avoid as primary chart in a11y contexts.
records.Color Guidance: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
records.Data Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
records.Keywords: part-to-whole, pie, donut, percentage, proportion, share
records.When NOT to Use: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
records.When to Use: ≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values

records.A11y Fallback: Data table with correlation coefficient annotation; shape markers (circle/square/triangle) per group
records.Accessibility Notes: Provide data table alternative. Combine color + shape distinction for colorblind users.
records.Color Guidance: Color axis: gradient (blue → red). Bubble size: relative to 3rd variable. Opacity: 0.6–0.8 to show density
records.Data Volume Threshold: <500 pts: SVG; 500–5000: Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
records.Keywords: correlation, distribution, scatter, relationship, pattern, cluster
records.When NOT to Use: Variables are categorical (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 points (patterns aren't meaningful); mobile-primary context
records.When to Use: Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset

records.A11y Fallback: Numerical overlay on hover; downloadable grid table with row/column labels
records.Accessibility Notes: Pattern overlay for colorblind users. Numerical value on hover. Legend must include scale ticks.
records.Color Guidance: Gradient: Cool (blue) to Hot (red). Divergent scale for ±data. Always include numeric color legend
records.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 10,000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
records.Keywords: heatmap, heat-map, intensity, density, matrix, calendar
records.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact values; colorblind users without pattern fallback
records.When to Use: Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (e.g., activity by hour × day)

records.A11y Fallback: Region text labels; sortable data table by region name and value; keyboard-navigable regions
records.Accessibility Notes: Include text labels for major regions. Provide keyboard navigation between regions.
records.Color Guidance: Single color gradient per region group. Categorized colors for discrete types. Legend with clear scale breaks
records.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 regions: SVG; ≥1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
records.Keywords: geographic, map, location, region, geo, spatial, choropleth
records.When NOT to Use: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
records.When to Use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user

records.A11y Fallback: Provide linear list view with stage name + count + drop-off %; keyboard traversal
records.Accessibility Notes: Explicit conversion % as text per stage. Stage labels always visible. Linear list view as fallback.
records.Color Guidance: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
records.Data Volume Threshold: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
records.Keywords: funnel, flow, conversion, drop-off, pipeline, stages
records.When NOT to Use: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
records.When to Use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages

records.A11y Fallback: Numerical value + % of target shown as visible text; ARIA live region for real-time updates
records.Accessibility Notes: Always show numerical value + % of target as text beside chart. Never rely on color position alone.
records.Color Guidance: Performance: Red → Yellow → Green gradient. Target: marker line. Threshold zones clearly differentiated
records.Data Volume Threshold: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
records.Keywords: performance, target, kpi, gauge, goal, threshold, progress
records.When NOT to Use: No target or benchmark exists; comparing multiple KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
records.When to Use: Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context

records.A11y Fallback: Toggle actual/forecast independently; legend labels must include line-style description
records.Accessibility Notes: Toggle between actual-only and forecast views. Legend must distinguish lines beyond color (solid vs dashed).
records.Color Guidance: Actual: solid line #0080FF. Forecast: dashed #FF9500. Confidence band: 15% opacity fill same hue
records.Data Volume Threshold: Keep historical window to 30–90 days for readability; forecast horizon ≤ 30% of visible x-axis range
records.Keywords: forecast, prediction, confidence, band, projection, estimate
records.When NOT to Use: No historical baseline; prediction confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
records.When to Use: Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders

records.A11y Fallback: Text alert annotation per anomaly; anomaly summary list panel alongside chart
records.Accessibility Notes: Use shape marker (not color only) for anomaly points. Add text annotation per anomaly event.
records.Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
records.Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
records.Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, detection, monitoring, deviation
records.When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
records.When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data

records.A11y Fallback: Collapsible tree table as primary view; treemap as supplementary visual only
records.Accessibility Notes: Poor baseline accessibility. Always provide table alternative as primary view. Label all large areas.
records.Color Guidance: Parent nodes: distinct hues. Children: lighter shades of same hue. White separator borders: 2–3px
records.Data Volume Threshold: <200 nodes: SVG; 200–1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
records.Keywords: hierarchy, nested, treemap, parent, children, breakdown, drill
records.When NOT to Use: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling values precisely
records.When to Use: Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., budget breakdown)

records.A11y Fallback: Flow table (Source → Target → Value); keyboard-traversable node list with tab stops
records.Accessibility Notes: Structural flow charts cannot be conveyed by color alone. Provide flow table. Avoid on mobile.
records.Color Guidance: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
records.Data Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
records.Keywords: flow, process, sankey, distribution, source, target, transfer
records.When NOT to Use: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
records.When to Use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution

records.A11y Fallback: Table with running total column; directional arrow icons per row
records.Accessibility Notes: Color + directional arrow icon per bar (not color alone). Labels on every bar.
records.Color Guidance: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
records.Data Volume Threshold: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
records.Keywords: waterfall, cumulative, variance, incremental, bridge, delta
records.When NOT to Use: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
records.When to Use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)

records.A11y Fallback: Grouped bar chart as mandatory alternative; include raw data table
records.Accessibility Notes: Limit axes to 5–8. Always provide grouped bar chart alternative for precise reading.
records.Color Guidance: Single dataset: #0080FF at 20% fill. Multiple: distinct hues with 30% fill. Border: full opacity
records.Data Volume Threshold: 2–3 datasets maximum per chart; 5–8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
records.Keywords: radar, spider, multi-variable, attributes, dimensions, comparison
records.When NOT to Use: Axes > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
records.When to Use: Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (e.g., product feature comparison)

records.A11y Fallback: OHLC data table with sortable columns; numeric summary panel (daily change %)
records.Accessibility Notes: Provide OHLC data table. Colorblind: use fill vs outline pattern (bullish = filled, bearish = hollow).
records.Color Guidance: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
records.Data Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
records.Keywords: stock, trading, ohlc, candlestick, finance, price, volume
records.When NOT to Use: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
records.When to Use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only

records.A11y Fallback: Adjacency list table (Node A → Node B → Weight); hierarchical tree view when structure allows
records.Accessibility Notes: Fundamentally inaccessible without alternative. Never use as sole representation. Always provide list alternative.
records.Color Guidance: Node types: categorical colors. Edges: #90A4AE at 60% opacity. Highlight path: #F59E0B
records.Data Volume Threshold: ≤100 nodes: SVG; 101–500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
records.Keywords: network, graph, nodes, edges, connections, relationships, force
records.When NOT to Use: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise connection counts; mobile context
records.When to Use: Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context

records.A11y Fallback: Stats summary table (min / Q1 / median / Q3 / max / mean); outlier count annotation
records.Accessibility Notes: Include stats summary table. Annotate outlier count in chart subtitle.
records.Color Guidance: Box fill: #BBDEFB. Border: #1976D2. Median line: #D32F2F bold. Outlier dots: #F44336
records.Data Volume Threshold: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is ⚡ Excellent at any volume
records.Keywords: distribution, statistical, spread, median, outlier, quartile, boxplot
records.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 data points per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
records.When to Use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups

records.A11y Fallback: Numerical values always visible (not hover-only); color ranges labeled with threshold text
records.Accessibility Notes: All values always visible as text. Color ranges are labeled with text thresholds not color alone.
records.Color Guidance: Qualitative ranges: #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9 (bad/ok/good). Performance bar: #1976D2. Target: black 3px marker
records.Data Volume Threshold: Ideal for 3–10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
records.Keywords: bullet, compact, kpi, dashboard, target, benchmark, range
records.When NOT to Use: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); data has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
records.When to Use: Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large

records.A11y Fallback: Percentage text always visible; grid cells labeled with aria-label value; provide legend
records.Accessibility Notes: Better than pie for accessibility. Percentage text label always visible. Each cell has aria-label.
records.Color Guidance: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
records.Data Volume Threshold: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
records.Keywords: waffle, percentage, proportion, progress, filled, grid
records.When NOT to Use: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
records.When to Use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format

records.A11y Fallback: Collapsible indented list with percentages; breadcrumb trail for current drill-down state
records.Accessibility Notes: Poor accessibility beyond 2 levels. Mandatory table alternative required for any production use.
records.Color Guidance: Center to outer: darker to lighter hue. Each level 15–20% lighter. Contrasting border between sectors
records.Data Volume Threshold: <100 nodes: SVG; 100–500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
records.Keywords: sunburst, hierarchy, nested, proportion, radial, circle
records.When NOT to Use: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
records.When to Use: Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., org spend breakdown)

records.A11y Fallback: Keyboard expand/collapse tree; screen reader announces node label + value + % impact
records.Accessibility Notes: Keyboard-navigable expand/collapse. Screen reader announces node value and % contribution.
records.Color Guidance: Positive impact nodes: #2563EB. Negative impact nodes: #EF4444. Neutral connectors: #94A3B8
records.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
records.Keywords: root cause, decomposition, tree, hierarchy, drill-down, ai-split, attribution
records.When NOT to Use: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
records.When to Use: Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios

records.A11y Fallback: Mandatory 2D projection view + data table; do not use as primary chart type in product UI
records.Accessibility Notes: 3D spatial charts are fundamentally inaccessible. Must not be used as primary chart type in any product UI.
records.Color Guidance: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
records.Data Volume Threshold: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
records.Keywords: 3d, spatial, immersive, terrain, molecular, volumetric, point-cloud
records.When NOT to Use: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
records.When to Use: Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D

records.A11y Fallback: Pause/resume button required; current value shown as large text KPI; prefers-reduced-motion: freeze animation
records.Accessibility Notes: Pause/resume control required. Current value as large visible text KPI. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
records.Color Guidance: Current pulse: #00FF00 (dark theme) or #0080FF (light theme). History: fading opacity. Grid: dark background
records.Data Volume Threshold: Canvas/WebGL required. Buffer last 60–300s of data. Downsample older data on scroll
records.Keywords: streaming, real-time, ticker, live, velocity, pulse, monitoring
records.When NOT to Use: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
records.When to Use: Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at ≥1 Hz; user needs current value at a glance

records.A11y Fallback: Sortable list view by frequency with sentiment label column; word cloud as supplementary only
records.Accessibility Notes: Word clouds fail screen readers. Never use as sole output of NLP analysis. Always pair with list view.
records.Color Guidance: Positive: #22C55E. Negative: #EF4444. Neutral: #94A3B8. Word size maps to frequency
records.Data Volume Threshold: 50–5000 terms optimal. Beyond 5000: apply top-N filtering before render. Avoid on mobile
records.Keywords: sentiment, emotion, nlp, opinion, feeling, text-analysis
records.When NOT to Use: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
records.When to Use: NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview

records.A11y Fallback: Path summary table (variant → frequency → avg duration); top 3 bottlenecks as text annotation panel
records.Accessibility Notes: Complex graphs are hard to navigate. Provide path summary text. Highlight top 3 bottlenecks as annotations.
records.Color Guidance: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
records.Data Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
records.Keywords: process, mining, variants, path, bottleneck, log, event
records.When NOT to Use: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
records.When to Use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels

records.Do: Use scrub: true or a small number (0.5-1.5) instead of instant jumps so it feels tied to the scrollbar

records.Keywords: route change, fade, page transition

records.Don't: Don't use shared-element transitions across more than one element pair per navigation; compounding Flips are hard to time correctly

records.Do: Keep the yPercent delta small (5-15) so foreground and background never desync distractingly

records.Do: Create all geometry before the animation loop; mutate BufferAttribute arrays in-place if needed
records.Don't: Call any new XxxGeometry() constructor inside the animation loop

records.Description: When multiple objects share the same shape create one geometry instance and pass it to every Mesh. Each Mesh gets its own transform and material while all share a single GPU buffer.
records.Do: Create one geometry and pass the same reference to every Mesh constructor
records.Don't: Create a separate identical geometry inside a loop for each object

records.Description: Call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() and texture.dispose() for every texture map when removing objects from the scene. Three.js never releases GPU resources automatically — they stay in VRAM until explicitly freed.
records.Do: Dispose of geometry + material + every texture map before calling scene.remove()
records.Don't: Call scene.remove() alone without any dispose calls

records.Description: Use the minimum segment count that achieves the desired silhouette quality. Hero objects: 32–64 segments. Background objects: 8–16. Particle stand-ins: 6–8. High counts on background geometry waste GPU draw calls with zero visible benefit.
records.Do: Apply a tiered segment budget based on the visual priority of each object in the scene
records.Don't: Default every sphere and cylinder to 64+ segments regardless of its role

records.Description: For any custom shape use BufferGeometry with setAttribute('position' ...) and a Float32Array. The legacy THREE.Geometry class was removed in r125 and throws ReferenceError in r128.
records.Do: Use THREE.BufferGeometry with a Float32Array position attribute for custom vertex data
records.Don't: Reference or instantiate the removed THREE.Geometry class

records.Description: MeshBasicMaterial ignores all lights and is significantly cheaper — use it for UI overlays HUDs and flat-colored decorative elements. MeshStandardMaterial is PBR-accurate and requires lights. Never use StandardMaterial where BasicMaterial suffices.
records.Do: Use MeshBasicMaterial for any object that does not need lighting; use MeshStandardMaterial for physical objects
records.Don't: Apply MeshStandardMaterial to flat UI elements that never receive light — lights still run for them

records.Description: Share one material instance across all meshes that have identical properties. Call mat.clone() only when individual meshes genuinely need different property values. Duplicate materials waste GPU VRAM.
records.Do: Assign the same material reference to all meshes with identical visual properties
records.Don't: Create a new material inside a loop for objects that look identical

records.Description: Textures are the single largest consumer of GPU VRAM in most Three.js scenes. Call texture.dispose() when switching scenes or removing objects — Three.js does not garbage-collect GPU resources automatically.
records.Do: Track all loaded textures and call dispose() on each one during scene teardown or on object removal
records.Don't: Load textures without any cleanup path — they persist in VRAM for the entire page lifetime

records.Description: Any scene using MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhongMaterial requires at minimum one AmbientLight (fill) and one DirectionalLight (shading direction). Without both the objects render as solid black — the material is there but no light reaches it.
records.Do: Add AmbientLight for fill and DirectionalLight for shading whenever PBR or Phong materials are used
records.Don't: Use MeshStandardMaterial without adding any lights to the scene

records.Description: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true must be set before any castShadow or receiveShadow flags. Without it the shadow map is never allocated and all shadow flags are silently ignored.
records.Do: Set renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true first then set castShadow and receiveShadow on lights and meshes
records.Don't: Set castShadow on a light or mesh without enabling renderer.shadowMap.enabled — shadows never render

records.Description: Shadow map rendering redraws the entire scene from the light's perspective every frame. Enable castShadow only on the primary directional light and receiveShadow only on hero meshes and the ground plane.
records.Do: Enable shadows only on the key light and the most important meshes
records.Don't: Enable castShadow and receiveShadow on every object in the scene including particles

records.Description: MeshBasicMaterial completely ignores all scene lights. Adding lights solely to illuminate BasicMaterial objects wastes a light pass on every frame with zero visible effect.
records.Do: Omit lights entirely when every material in the scene is MeshBasicMaterial
records.Don't: Add AmbientLight and DirectionalLight to a scene that uses only MeshBasicMaterial

records.Description: Create exactly one Raycaster instance outside all event handlers. Store mouse coordinates in pointermove (cheap). Call setFromCamera and intersectObjects together inside the animate() loop — once per frame instead of once per mouse event.
records.Do: Create one Raycaster; store mouse in pointermove; call setFromCamera + intersectObjects inside animate()
records.Don't: Create a new THREE.Raycaster() inside a mousemove handler or call setFromCamera inside the event listener

records.Description: Raycasting requires mouse in Normalized Device Coordinates: X from -1 (left) to +1 (right) and Y from +1 (top) to -1 (bottom). The Y axis is inverted relative to screen space. A missing negation on Y causes all raycasts to miss or hit the wrong objects.
records.Do: Apply the full NDC formula — including the negation on the Y axis
records.Don't: Forget to negate Y — raycasting appears to work but hits objects mirrored vertically

records.Description: Call raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse camera) and then raycaster.intersectObjects(targets true) inside the animate() loop. setFromCamera must come before intersectObjects every frame — without it the raycaster uses a stale ray direction.
records.Do: Call setFromCamera then intersectObjects in order inside every animate() frame
records.Don't: Call intersectObjects without calling setFromCamera first — the raycaster uses a stale or zero ray

records.Description: Pass true as the second argument to intersectObjects when testing Groups or GLTF loaded models. Geometry lives on child Mesh objects — without recursive:true the parent group is tested but has no geometry and hits is always empty.
records.Do: Use intersectObjects(targets true) for Groups or any loaded model
records.Don't: Raycast against a parent Group without the recursive flag
records.Guideline: Recursive Flag for Groups and GLTF

records.Description: Set document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer' when intersections are found and reset to 'auto' when none are found. Without cursor feedback users cannot discover that 3D objects are interactive.
records.Do: Update cursor to pointer on hit; reset to auto on miss in the same animate loop block
records.Don't: Run raycasting and read hits without ever updating the cursor style

records.Description: Drive the render loop exclusively with requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop(). Never use setInterval or setTimeout — they are not synchronized to the display refresh rate and keep running when the tab is hidden draining battery.
records.Do: Use requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the sole render loop driver
records.Don't: Use setInterval or setTimeout for render timing

records.Description: Use THREE.Clock and clock.getDelta() for all time-based motion. A hardcoded increment like += 0.01 runs at 2x speed on 120Hz displays and at unpredictable speed when frames drop under load. CRITICAL: call getDelta() exactly ONCE per animate() frame and store the result in a local dt variable. getDelta() resets the internal clock on every call — a second call in the same frame always returns ~0, silently breaking any animation block that uses it.
records.Do: Call clock.getDelta() once at the top of animate(); store result in dt; reuse dt everywhere in that frame
records.Don't: Call clock.getDelta() more than once per frame or inside a helper called from animate()

records.Description: Use value += (target - value) * alpha each frame to smoothly interpolate toward a moving target. An alpha of 0.03–0.1 produces organic easing for camera follow pointer-tracking and hover scale effects without requiring GSAP.
records.Do: Apply the lerp formula each frame with a small alpha for smooth organic motion
records.Don't: Snap a value directly to the target producing an instant jarring jump

records.Description: Use GSAP timelines for any animation with more than two sequential steps or for scroll-linked camera paths. GSAP timelines can be paused reversed and scrubbed — far more maintainable than boolean state machines.
records.Do: Use GSAP timelines for sequences with more than two steps and for scroll-driven animations
records.Don't: Implement multi-step sequences with boolean flags and manual frame counters

records.Description: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the loop driver so you can pass null to pause and a function to resume. Continuous rendering in a hidden tab wastes CPU GPU and battery with no user benefit.
records.Do: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate) to drive the loop; pass null to pause on visibilitychange
records.Don't: Drive with internal requestAnimationFrame and never stop the loop when the tab is hidden
records.Guideline: Pause Render Loop on Tab Hidden

records.Description: Load GSAP from its own CDN script tag before your scene script. In bundler projects install via npm and import. GSAP is a completely separate library from Three.js — never try to import it from the Three.js package.
records.Do: Load GSAP CDN before the scene script; or npm install gsap and import separately
records.Don't: Import gsap from three or expect it to be defined without a separate load

records.Description: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) once at the top of your script before any scrollTrigger config object. Without registration the ScrollTrigger name is undefined and the tween throws immediately.
records.Do: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) as the first line before any gsap.to/from/timeline with scrollTrigger
records.Don't: Include scrollTrigger config in gsap.to() calls without first registering the plugin

records.Description: GSAP can tween any numeric JavaScript property including mesh.position.x mesh.rotation.y and material.opacity. No wrapper or adaptor is needed. Note: to tween material.opacity the material must have transparent:true set before the tween starts.
records.Do: Pass Three.js object properties directly to gsap.to(); set transparent:true before tweening opacity
records.Don't: Use a plain proxy object then manually copy values to Three.js properties every frame

records.Description: Use scrub:true or scrub:1 to link camera movement continuously to scroll position as a 0–1 ratio. scrub:1 adds a 1-second lag for cinematic smoothness. onEnter/onLeave fire only once and create jarring snaps — not the right tool for a camera path.
records.Do: Use scrub:1 for any scroll-controlled camera movement
records.Don't: Use onEnter or onLeave callbacks for camera motion — they snap instead of scrubbing

records.Description: Use THREE.InstancedMesh when rendering 50 or more identical objects. It submits all N transforms in one draw call instead of N draw calls and reduces CPU-GPU communication overhead dramatically.
records.Do: Use InstancedMesh for any group of 50+ meshes sharing the same geometry and material
records.Don't: Create 50+ separate Mesh objects with the same geometry and material

records.Description: Enable ACESFilmicToneMapping and sRGBEncoding on the renderer for accurate perceptual color. Without tone mapping colors appear washed out or over-saturated. These are renderer properties set after construction and take effect immediately.
records.Do: Set renderer.toneMapping and renderer.outputEncoding after construction for all production scenes
records.Don't: Leave tone mapping and output encoding at defaults when the scene targets realistic visuals

records.Description: The antialias option can only be set at WebGLRenderer construction time. Setting renderer.antialias after construction has absolutely no effect — the WebGL context is already created without it. Decide before instantiating.
records.Do: Set antialias:true inside the WebGLRenderer constructor options object
records.Don't: Construct the renderer without antialias then try to enable it by assigning the property

records.Description: Use scene.fog to create atmospheric depth. As a secondary benefit objects that disappear into fog before the far plane stop contributing to draw calls — useful in scenes with large view distances.
records.Do: Add FogExp2 to scenes with view distances above 100 units for both visual atmosphere and implicit far culling
records.Don't: Ignore fog in scenes with far:1000+ and many distant objects that contribute tiny pixels per draw call
records.Guideline: FogExp2 for Depth and Far Culling

records.Description: Build all particle systems with BufferGeometry plus a Float32Array position attribute rendered as Points. Never use individual Mesh objects as particles — they cannot scale past a few hundred with good performance.
records.Do: Use Points plus BufferGeometry for all particle effects
records.Don't: Create hundreds of individual Mesh objects to simulate a particle system
records.Guideline: BufferGeometry Plus Points for Particle Systems

records.Description: Start particle systems at 1000–3000 particles. Beyond 50000 causes sustained frame drops on mid-range mobile. Always test on a real device before increasing the count — desktop and mobile GPU performance ratios can be 10:1.
records.Do: Start at 3000 particles and profile on actual mobile hardware before raising the limit
records.Don't: Set particle count at 100000 or higher without any mobile profiling

records.Description: After mutating any BufferAttribute array values per frame you must set geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true so Three.js re-uploads the changed buffer to the GPU. Without it the GPU still uses the old data and particles appear completely frozen.
records.Do: Set needsUpdate = true on the position attribute after every per-frame mutation of the array
records.Don't: Mutate the Float32Array values without flagging needsUpdate — positions update in JS but not on the GPU

records.Description: Size the renderer and camera to the canvas element's clientWidth and clientHeight — not window.innerWidth and innerHeight. This is correct when the canvas is inside a flex or grid container that does not fill the full viewport.
records.Do: Use canvas.clientWidth and canvas.clientHeight for all renderer and camera sizing
records.Don't: Hardcode renderer size to window.innerWidth/innerHeight when the canvas may be inside a container

records.Description: Use ResizeObserver on the canvas container instead of the window resize event. ResizeObserver fires when the container element changes size independently of the browser window — common in split-pane layouts and sidebar collapsing.
records.Do: Attach ResizeObserver to the canvas parent element for accurate container-aware resize detection
records.Don't: Use only window.addEventListener('resize') for canvas sizing when the canvas is not fullscreen

records.Description: Add touchstart and touchmove listeners alongside mouse events so the scene remains interactive on mobile. Normalize touch coordinates to the same NDC range as mouse events and pass passive:false on touchmove if you call preventDefault.
records.Do: Handle both mouse and touch input for any interactive 3D scene
records.Don't: Add only mouse event listeners and leave touch users with no interaction

records.Description: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') before starting any auto-rotation, particle animation, or camera movement. Users who enable this OS preference have motion sickness or vestibular disorders. IMPORTANT: reading .matches once at page load is a one-time snapshot — if the user changes their OS accessibility setting mid-session the scene will not react. Attach a 'change' listener to the MediaQueryList so noMotion stays in sync at runtime.
records.Do: Use matchMedia.addEventListener('change') to keep noMotion reactive; gate all auto-animation on the live value
records.Don't: Read .matches once at startup and never update it — the scene ignores mid-session OS setting changes

records.Description: Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label to renderer.domElement after appending it to the DOM. Screen readers receive no information from a WebGL canvas — the aria-label is the only description they can announce to users.
records.Do: Set role='img' and a meaningful aria-label on renderer.domElement before or after appending it
records.Don't: Append the canvas to the DOM with no accessibility attributes — invisible to screen readers

records.Description: For production use Three.js via npm plus Vite. You get full tree-shaking reduced bundle size access to the complete examples/jsm library including OrbitControls GLTFLoader and EffectComposer and TypeScript support.
records.Do: Use npm install three plus Vite or Webpack for any production client-facing project
records.Don't: Serve raw CDN script tags in a production application that needs tree-shaking or TypeScript

records.Description: Load 3D models using GLTFLoader and traverse gltf.scene to configure castShadow receiveShadow and material overrides on all child Mesh nodes. Calling scene.add(gltf.scene) alone silently skips all shadow and material configuration.
records.Do: Use GLTFLoader and traverse the entire gltf.scene graph to set up shadows and materials on every Mesh child
records.Don't: Load a GLTF model and pass gltf.scene directly to scene.add without traversing child meshes

records.Description: Use THREE.LOD to automatically swap high-detail and low-detail geometry as objects move closer or farther from the camera. This maintains frame rate in scenes with many objects spread across a large depth range.
records.Do: Use THREE.LOD to reduce triangle count on distant objects automatically
records.Don't: Render the same high-polygon geometry for every object regardless of its distance from the camera
